CEREMONIAL MATTERS  Mayor Tomek requested that the meeting be adjourned in memory
  of those that have suffered due to death and illness caused by
  COVID-19; all first responders and individuals suffering due to the
  wild fires throughout California; and the victims of recent gun
  violence in the City.

  Mayor Tomek introduced and welcomed the new Sergeant-at-
  Arms, Sergeant Thomas Blanchard, and extended appreciation to
  Sergeant Monica Cuellar for her service.

  Mayor Tomek recognized and spoke on Hispanic & Latino
  Heritage Month, from September 15, 2020 through October 15,
  2020, and read a proclamation honoring its importance to the City
  and community members.

  Vice Mayor Hampton, and Councilmembers Gordo, and Kennedy
  spoke on the need to visually recognize Hispanic & Latino
  Heritage month abiding by social distancing regulations and safety
  measures. Councilmember Gordo requested that the Pasadena
  Central Library commence a reading program or highlight
  movies/documentaries as an effort to raise awareness and
  recognize the contributions of Latinos; and to continue such a
  program with all heritages that make up the community of
  Pasadena.

  Steve Mermell, City Manager responded that he would meet with
  staff to determine alternative methods to commemorate Hispanic
  & Latino Heritage month. He provided an update on the Los
  Angeles Bobcat Fire, including information on evacuation orders
  and warnings to effected city residents, and responded to
  questions.

  Councilmembers Kennedy and Gordo, and Vice Mayor Hampton
  spoke on recent gun violence in the City, specifically the shooting
  of two minors, and the shooting of two Los Angeles Police Officers,
  and on Pasadena Police Officers' efforts to keep the community
  safe. Council member Gordo spoke in favor of the City joining with
  the City of Los Angeles in asking for peace.

DEPARTMENTS  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council

  AUTHORIZATION TO ENTER INTO A CONTRACT WITH MIG
  FOR AN AMOUNT NOT-TO-EXCEED $374,655 TO PROVIDE
  CONSULTING SERVICES FOR THE PREPARATION OF THE
  2021-2029 HOUSING ELEMENT UPDATE
  Recommendation: It is recommended that the City Council:
  (1) Find that the action proposed in the agenda report is not a
  project subject to the California Environmental Quality Act
  ("CEQA") as defined in Section 21065 of CEQA and the State
  CEQA Guidelines Section 15060(c)(2), 15060(c)(3), and 15378;
  and
  (2) Authorize the City Manager to enter into a contract as a result
  of a competitive selection process pursuant to Pasadena
  Municipal Code Section 4.08.047 with MIG for an amount not-to-
  exceed $374,655 for the preparation of the 2021-2029 Housing
  Element update. (Contract No. 31843)

  The two above agenda items were discussed concurrently.

  David Reyes, Director of Planning and Community Development,
  provided introductory comments, and Arlene Granadosin-Jones,
  City Planner, presented a PowerPoint presentation on the item,
  with both responding to questions.

  Councilmember Gordo spoke in favor of utilizing the same
  consultant that is being recommended to assist the City with the
  preparation of the 2021-2029 Housing Element update, to develop
  an appeal on the Regional Housing Needs Assessment (RHNA)
  allocations. He spoke in favor of appealing the RHNA's allocation,
  and consider joining with other large municipalities, including cities
  in the region and the San Gabriel Valley. He also spoke in favor of
  joining surrounding municipalities in litigation action against
  Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) for the
  unachievable allocation numbers and encroachment into local
  control. He expressed strong concerns regarding the unfair
  treatment of Pasadena in light of other cities that have not made
  good faith efforts to construct affordable housing towards the
  regional housing goals. He spoke in favor of rejoining the San
  Gabriel Valley Council of Governments and partnering with
  surrounding cities to advocate as a region.

  Councilmembers Masuda and Wilson spoke in favor of
  challenging the COG in setting unrealistic and unattainable
  RHNA's allocations.

Council Minutes  16  09/14/2020
   Councilmember McAustin spoke in favor of challenging the
  RHNA'a allocations on several levels, appealing the RHNA's
  allocations, and the need to continue to approach the City's land
  use on a sustainability basis. In addition, she also spoke on the
  need to educate the California Department of Housing and
  Community Development (HCD), in a meaningful and methodical
  manner, on the City's support of housing within the scope of a
  sustainable community, the City's track record in building
  affordable housing (in comparison to other municipalities), and the
  City's desire to provide its share of affordable housing within the
  confines of the City's ability to provide such housing.

  City Manager Mermell suggested that the City Council consider
  approving an additional allocation of $30,000 with MIG (separate
  item on the agenda for preparation of the City's 2021-2029
  Housing Element) to allow the consultant to provide advice and
  preparation of the RHNA allocation appeal.

  Councilmember Madison expressed concerns with RHNA
  allocation that mandates the City to severely increase housing
  density and impact the character of the community; and spoke in
  favor of appealing the RHNA allocation and all options, including
  litigation, becoming part of a consortium cities for this effort, and
  lobbying the State's legislative bodies including the State Senate.
  Councilmember Kennedy requested that staff provide information
  to the City Council on the pros and cons of filing a RHNA allocation
  appeal. He spoke on the need for the City Council to make a policy
  decision to build one thousand units of housing in a three-year
  period . The units should be for extremely-low, very-low, and low
  income salary categories.
